thread:
Sam: Heads-up — compliance asked for a slimmer streaming delivery for audit events. They want to be able to reconstruct "who changed what" for routing policies / quota rules. Do we have a proposed minimal shape that covers before/after, actor, and request context?

Maria: For the console UX we also need a very small join key so we can show 'change trail' inline without fetching giant blobs. Maybe store a short change_id + pointer to full payload.

Ashley: +1 on pointer. For exports I think NDJSON lines are ideal (one event per line) and we gzip. We should include a tiny header object in the stream for schema_version. Example: `{"schema":"audit.v1","generated_by":"redwood-auditd"}` followed by events.

Kevin: I worry about immutability guarantees. If we include before/after diffs we either need to keep full snapshots or store deltas plus a patch algorithm. Deltas are smaller but harder to replay reliably. Thoughts?

Sam: The replay requirement is real — auditors want deterministic state at time T. Maybe we mandate that any change to a routing policy emits both the 'patch' and a compact 'effective_state' for the changed resource (not full org snapshot, just the resource). That keeps size bounded.

Maria: That would map nicely to the console: we can render a small inline diff and link to the effective_state JSON if they click "expand". Also helps rollouts UX — show which rollout changed a routing rule and why.

Ashley: Operational notes: when streaming to S3 we should rotate files by size and include manifest files with last_event_ts. Consumers can tail manifests to discover new files. Also we need an option for Kinesis/Kafka for real-time customers.

Kevin: Schema suggestion (super-minimal):
```
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "ts": "iso8601",
  "actor": {"id": "u123", "email": "alice@redwood.ai", "role": "platform-admin"},
  "resource": {"type": "routing_policy", "id": "rp-42"},
  "change": {"type": "update", "diff": {"path":"/rules/0/priority","from":1,"to":2}, "effective_state": { /* compact resource */ } },
  "meta": {"source":"console|api|cli","ip":"1.2.3.4","request_id":"r-abc"}
}
```

Sam: That looks good. Can we add a `scope` field for tenancy (org/team) and `retention_tier` so exports can be filtered for compliance retention?

Ashley: Add retention_tier yes. Also we should include `encrypted_at_rest":true` in the manifest metadata for exporters.

compliance-bot: Reminder: retention rules differ by region. Events that are put into S3 with eu- region flags must adhere to EU retention policies. Use `region` in manifest.

Kevin: Another internal API debate — should we normalize `actor` to always be a compact user object or allow `service` and `system` types with different fields? I prefer a union type but for JSON we should keep the fields predictable: `actor.type` = one of ["user","service","system"] and a flattened set of optional fields.

Maria: UX question — can we include a `ui_hint` array in events (e.g., ["show-diff","show-rollback"]) so console can decide what actions to surface without hardcoding rules?

Sam: Nice. That decouples UI from schema. Ok next steps: Kevin/Ashley to draft a 1-pager with exact json shape + retention/manifest rules. Maria will sketch console wireframes that reference `change.event_id` and `effective_state`. I'll sync with Compliance after that.

Ashley: I'll drop a PR for the exporter CLI (redwood-cli audit export --stream) and include NDJSON demo. Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow. 🤖

Kevin: I'll work on versioning plan (schema v1 + migration doc). Plan to include `schema_version` in every file header.

Maria: Thanks all — this will unblock the rollout auditing story. 👍
